milestones.title: Sultan Majid plans a new town at Mzizima
milestones.detail: Sultan Majid bin Said of Zanzibar decided to build a town on the bay beside the fishing village of Mzizima and named it Dar es Salaam. Building began in 1865 or 1866.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica (1911), 'Dar-es-Salaam', https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Dar-es-Salaam; Brennan & Burton (2007), 'The Emerging Metropolis', via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar_es_Salaam

milestones.title: Old Boma completed
milestones.detail: The Old Boma, built in 1866-67 close to the sultan's palace, is one of the oldest surviving buildings in the city.

milestones.title: Majid dies and the town declines
milestones.detail: After Sultan Majid's death in 1870 his palace was left unfinished and the new town fell into decline for nearly two decades.
milestones.source: Brennan & Burton (2007), 'The Emerging Metropolis: A history of Dar es Salaam, circa 1862-2000', via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar_es_Salaam

milestones.title: German East Africa Company station
milestones.detail: Carl Peters occupied the town for the German East Africa Company in 1887 and set up a station, which revived the settlement.

milestones.title: Capital of German East Africa
milestones.detail: The German colonial administration moved its seat from Bagamoyo to Dar es Salaam in 1891.

milestones.title: Lutheran church and Catholic cathedral finished
milestones.detail: The Lutheran church on the harbour front (now Azania Front) and St Joseph's Cathedral, both begun in the late 1890s, were completed by 1902 and still mark the old German town centre.
milestones.source: https://www.azaniafront.org/history and Michael Hodd, East Africa Handbook, p. 344, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar_es_Salaam

milestones.title: Railway reaches Morogoro
milestones.detail: The first section of the Central Railway, from Dar es Salaam to Morogoro, was built by 1907.

milestones.title: Central Railway reaches Kigoma
milestones.detail: The line from Dar es Salaam to Kigoma on Lake Tanganyika began operating, making the town the port for the whole interior.

milestones.title: Captured by British forces
milestones.detail: After naval bombardment in July and August, the German authorities surrendered the town on 3 September 1916. It became the capital of the British Tanganyika Territory.
milestones.source: Conrad Cato (1919), The Navy Everywhere, ch. XII, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar_es_Salaam

milestones.title: Becomes a municipality
milestones.detail: The township was raised to a municipality in 1949 with a nominated council and a mayor, during the rapid growth that followed the Second World War.
milestones.source: John Iliffe (1979), A Modern History of Tanganyika, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar_es_Salaam

milestones.title: Capital of independent Tanganyika
milestones.detail: Tanganyika became independent in December 1961 with Dar es Salaam as its capital. It stayed the capital when Tanzania was formed in 1964.

milestones.title: Decision to move the capital to Dodoma
milestones.detail: Provision was made in 1973 to move the national capital inland to Dodoma. Most government offices nevertheless stayed in Dar es Salaam for decades.

milestones.title: TAZARA Railway opens
milestones.detail: The TAZARA Railway began operating in 1975, giving the port a second trunk line into the interior.

milestones.title: National Assembly moves to Dodoma
milestones.detail: The transfer of the capital was officially completed in 1996 when parliament moved to Dodoma. Dar es Salaam remained the commercial capital and largest city.

milestones.title: Kigamboni (Nyerere) Bridge opens
milestones.detail: The 680 m bridge to Kigamboni, with a 200 m main span, opened in April 2016.

milestones.title: Tanzanite Bridge opens
milestones.detail: The 1.03 km Tanzanite Bridge, with a 670 m main span, opened on 1 February 2022.

notes: Start date: sources disagree by a few years. The 1911 Britannica and most reference works date Sultan Majid's decision to 1862; Brennan and Burton say building began in 1865 or 1866, and the Old Boma dates from 1866-67. 1862 is used. The older village of Mzizima on the same shore is undated. Population: no censuses before 1948 were found in primary form. All earlier points are rounded figures from two German secondary works (Hecklau 1989, Speitkamp 2005) and the 1911 Britannica, read through the German Wikipedia table, so they are marked 'estimated'; the 1887 point is the midpoint of a published range. The 1867 figure comes from a municipal profile and is the weakest. The 1909 Britannica estimate (24,000) is slightly above the 1913 figure (22,500), which shows the looseness of these estimates rather than a real fall. The 1921 and 1931 figures correspond to British census years but were only found rounded. Landmarks: all six entries date from 2012 or later. No sourced height was found for any colonial-era building, so these were left out: Old Boma (1867), Azania Front Lutheran Church (1902), St Joseph's Cathedral (1902), Ocean Road Hospital (1897), State House (1922), Askari Monument, Kilimanjaro Hotel (1965), Benjamin Mkapa Stadium, and the Kigamboni and Tanzanite bridges (no pylon heights). Two heights (Uhuru Heights, Rita Tower) are CTBUH estimates. Four towers could not be found on OpenStreetMap or Wikipedia, so their coordinates are street-level points from their CTBUH street addresses and should be checked before close-up rendering.
